hints: Remember what each test is really looking for, 2,4-DNPH finds the carbonyl group while alkaline iodine finds something more specific.
2,4-DNPH gives an orange precipitate with both aldehydes and ketones, so check which options actually contain a C=O group.
Alkaline aqueous iodine gives a yellow precipitate only with a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, so look for the carbonyl that also has a methyl next to it.
walkthrough:
**What does 2,4-DNPH tell us?**

2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine gives an orange-yellow precipitate with any aldehyde or ketone. It is a test for the carbonyl group, $\text{C=O}$.

$$\text{RCHO or RCOR'} + \text{2,4-DNPH} \rightarrow \text{orange precipitate}$$

**What does alkaline aqueous iodine tell us?**

Alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ is the iodoform test. It gives a pale yellow precipitate of triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$, only when the molecule has a methyl carbonyl group.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}- \text{group} + \text{I}_2 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3(s) \text{ yellow precipitate}$$

**Combine both conditions**

We need a compound that is an aldehyde or ketone AND contains $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$. That means we need a methyl ketone. Ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, would also work, but it is not listed.

$$\text{required structure: } \text{CH}_3-\text{C(=O)}-$$

**Check the four compounds**

Butanone is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It has a carbonyl for DNPH and it is a methyl ketone for iodoform, so it passes both tests.

options.A: Butan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is a secondary alcohol with no carbonyl group, so it gives no precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. It fails the first test, so it cannot be correct even though the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit can be oxidised to give a positive iodoform result.
options.B: Butanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, is an aldehyde so it does give an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. However it has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, it is not a methyl carbonyl, so it gives no yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate with alkaline iodine.
options.C: Butanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is a ketone so it gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. It is also a methyl ketone containing $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so it gives a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline aqueous iodine. It passes both tests.
options.D: Pentan-3-one, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is a ketone so it does give an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. However the carbonyl is flanked by two ethyl groups, not a methyl group, so it is not a methyl ketone and gives a negative iodoform test.
